# API environment

<!-- Generated by `moon run api:env-docs` from apps/api/src/config/environment; do not edit. -->

`SNAPFLOW_ENVIRONMENT` selects the deployment profile: whether the deployment is hosted (HTTPS origins, loopback Vault Proxy, verified database TLS, no localhost domain, no test keys) and whether logs and audit entries go to a developer console. Every application value comes from the environment, and code holds no deployment values: a local apps/api/.env (gitignored; it lists every variable development may set, in the sections below, and an empty value counts as unset) sets them in development; in production Kubernetes sets them from OpenBao through the External Secrets Operator. Secrets have no default. Runtime settings live in the settings system, and policy in versioned `*_POLICY` constants.

## Environment

The deployment selector and the process role

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SNAPFLOW_ENVIRONMENT` | development \| production |  | all |  | The deployment profile: development or production. |
| `SNAPFLOW_PROCESS_ROLE` | api \| worker \| all |  |  |  | What this process runs (api, worker or all); Kubernetes and moon set it for every API process. |

## Observability

Logging and tracing

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | trace \| debug \| info \| warn \| error \| fatal | info |  |  | Pino log level; debug also logs HTTP requests and times @LogExecution methods. |
| `SQL_LOG_LEVEL` | trace \| debug \| info \| warn \| error \| fatal |  | all |  | Most verbose log level that still logs SQL statements: they are logged while LOG_LEVEL is at or below it. |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | string |  |  |  | OTLP/HTTP collector the traces are exported to; tracing is off without it. The standard OTEL_* variables tune the exporter. |

## Public URLs & Domain

The public origins of the API, website and dashboard, and the sandbox domain

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `API_URL` | string |  | production |  | Public origin of the API; hosted deployments require HTTPS. |
| `WEBSITE_URL` | string |  | production |  | Public origin of the marketing website. |
| `ADMIN_URL` | string |  | production |  | Public origin of the dashboard (served under /dashboard). |
| `SNAPFLOW_PLATFORM_DOMAIN` | string |  | production |  | Domain under which sandboxes are exposed; hosted deployments refuse a localhost domain or one sharing a site with API_URL, ADMIN_URL or WEBSITE_URL. |
| `SNAPFLOW_EDGE_HTTPS_PORT` | string |  | only development |  | HTTPS port of the local edge in sandbox origins; hosted edges serve the default 443. |
| `SNAPFLOW_EDGE_GUEST_ORIGIN` | string |  | only development |  | Origin at which sandbox guests reach the local edge for speedtests; hosted guests reach each edge at https://<its public host>. |

## Network & Proxies

The HTTP listener and the proxies in front of it

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PORT` | string | 3001 |  |  | TCP port the HTTP API listens on. |
| `SNAPFLOW_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` | string | 127.0.0.0/8,::1/128 |  |  | Proxies whose X-Forwarded-For the API trusts. |

## Social sign-in

OAuth applications for Google and GitHub sign-in; a provider is offered only when both of its variables are set

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | string |  |  |  | Client ID of the Google OAuth application. |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | string |  |  | yes | Client secret of the Google OAuth application. |
| `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` | string |  |  |  | Client ID of the GitHub OAuth application. |
| `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` | string |  |  | yes | Client secret of the GitHub OAuth application. |

## Database

PostgreSQL; one-off processes (migrations, CLI) use a single connection

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | string |  | all | yes | PostgreSQL connection URL; each deployment has its own database. TLS follows its libpq sslmode and sslrootcert parameters; hosted deployments require sslmode=verify-full. |
| `DATABASE_POOL_MAX` | string |  | all |  | Maximum pooled connections of each long-running API or worker process. |
| `DATABASE_POOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` | string |  | all |  | Milliseconds an idle pooled connection stays open before it is closed. |
| `DATABASE_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS` | string |  | all |  | Milliseconds to wait for a new database connection before failing. |

## Redis

Redis: locks, throttling, realtime fan-out and caches

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `REDIS_URL` | string |  | all | yes | Redis URL redis://[user:password@]host:port (rediss:// for TLS), without a database index: the API uses databases 0 and 1. |

## Email

Transactional email sent through Resend

In development, set RESEND_BASE_URL to the devcontainer Resend emulator and any re_ key to capture email locally; without RESEND_API_KEY the API starts but every email send fails.

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RESEND_API_KEY` | string |  | production | yes | Resend API key with sending access to the EMAIL_FROM domain. |
| `EMAIL_FROM` | string |  | production |  | Sender of platform email on a domain verified in Resend, as an address or "Display Name <address>"; required with RESEND_API_KEY. |
| `EMAIL_REPLY_TO` | string |  |  |  | Reply-To address of platform email. |
| `RESEND_BASE_URL` | string |  | only development |  | Origin of a local Resend API emulator that captures email instead of sending it; unset sends through https://api.resend.com. |

## Object Storage

S3-compatible object storage for build contexts, logs and backups

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `S3_ENDPOINT` | string |  |  |  | Endpoint of a self-hosted S3-compatible object storage with STS AssumeRole support; setting it selects that provider and requires S3_ACCESS_KEY and S3_SECRET_KEY, and without it the AWS S3 endpoint is derived from S3_REGION. |
| `S3_REGION` | string |  | production |  | S3 signing region; without S3_ENDPOINT it selects the AWS S3 endpoint. |
| `S3_DEFAULT_BUCKET` | string |  | production |  | Bucket of platform objects. |
| `S3_ACCESS_KEY` | string |  |  | yes | Static S3 access key, set with S3_SECRET_KEY; required with S3_ENDPOINT, otherwise the AWS default credential chain applies. |
| `S3_SECRET_KEY` | string |  |  | yes | Static S3 secret key. |
| `S3_ROLE_ARN` | string |  |  |  | IAM role AWS STS assumes to issue push credentials scoped to an organization; required for AWS S3 and not allowed with S3_ENDPOINT. |
| `SNAPFLOW_VOLUME_BACKUP_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | string | 900 |  |  | Seconds between incremental backups of the volumes of a running sandbox; a host failure loses at most this much volume data. |

## Cloudflare

Custom domains through the Cloudflare zone of the platform domain

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SNAPFLOW_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` | string |  | production | yes | Cloudflare API token with Zone:Read, DNS:Edit and SSL and Certificates:Edit on the platform domain's zone; the zone and its custom hostname fallback origin (the custom domains' CNAME target) are looked up with it. |
| `SNAPFLOW_CLOUDFLARE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | string |  | production | yes | Shared secret of Cloudflare custom hostname webhooks. |
